title: Falcon 9 Starlink Group 15-16 (27 V2 Mini Optimized, SLC-4E)

azimuth_deg.derived: launch-plane azimuth tuned (2026-10-25) so the simulated orbit plane reaches i=70.007 deg (SpaceX pre-launch state vector via CelesTrak SupGP): the textbook inertial azimuth 180-asin(cos i/cos lat)=155.45 deg gave i=69.67 deg in the sim because the sim's steering plane is applied to the Earth-rotating launch state; +0.42 deg corrects it
azimuth_deg.src: https://celestrak.org/NORAD/elements/supplemental/sup-gp.php?FILE=starlink-g15-16&FORMAT=json (CelesTrak SupGP 'Starlink G15-16 Pre-Launch', derived from a pre-launch state vector provided by SpaceX; epoch 2026-10-27T05:47:17.38Z)
azimuth_deg.check: inside hazard corridor: NAVAREA XII 737/26 Hazard Area A (alternate window 270445Z-270910Z OCT covers T0) far edge spans bearings 151.8-157.3 deg from the pad (centre 154.56 deg, used for the surrogate) https://space-notices.com/notice/nav-warning-NAVAREA%20XII%20737%2F26

payload_kg.note: FITTED within 13.0-21.6 t so the published SECO-1 time delivers the SpaceX-sourced parking orbit; SpaceX does not publish Starlink stack mass

insertion_alt_km.derived: perigee of SECO-1 parking orbit: SECO-1 (T+8:39) at perigee, SES-2 (T+53:01) at apogee per SpaceX timeline -> coast 2662 s = half period -> a=6590.0 km; r_p = 2a - r_a

apoapsis_alt_km.src: https://celestrak.org/NORAD/elements/supplemental/sup-gp.php?FILE=starlink-g15-16&FORMAT=json (CelesTrak SupGP 'Starlink G15-16 Pre-Launch', derived from a pre-launch state vector provided by SpaceX; epoch 2026-10-27T05:47:17.38Z): deploy orbit 252.1 x 264.7 km (mean elements, above equatorial radius), i 70.007 deg; SES-2 at apogee raises perigee only, so parking apogee = deploy apogee (DERIVED)

target.altitude_reference: equatorial-radius (r - 6378.137 km) for SMA; insertion altitude residual uses geodetic altitude (~3 km difference at ~22N, accepted via 1 km-weight)

header_notes: Not flown: LL2 NET 2026-10-27T04:45Z (Mon Oct 26 9:45 pm PDT), status Go; Spaceflight Now agrees (B1082.26, OCISLY). File continues past SECO-1 through SES-2/SECO-2 to payload deploy (POST-CUTOFF lines).
Published timeline (SpaceX): Max-Q 1:08, MECO 2:26, stage sep 2:30, SES-1 2:36, fairing 2:56, SECO-1 8:39, SES-2 53:01, SECO-2 53:03, deploy 1:01:53.
Target orbit: SpaceX pre-launch state vector (CelesTrak SupGP starlink-g15-16): deploy 252 x 265 km, i 70.007 deg. Deploy epoch 05:47:17Z = T+1:02:17 vs SpaceX page 1:01:53 (24 s, noted).

knots.src: https://github.com/shahar603/Telemetry-Data/tree/master/Iridium%20NEXT%207 (SpaceX webcast telemetry; FAMILY stand-in, not this flight)

fitted.method: scipy least_squares (TRF, bounded) vs published knots + target orbit

payload_kg.basis: 27 V2 Mini Optimized: ~575 kg each community-reported (spacex.com.pl) = 15.5 t; MaxQ lists 800 kg each = 21.6 t (upper bound). Mass not published by SpaceX

cd.assumption: same Cd as the ascent fit (fixed 0.4)

burns.name: SES-2/SECO-2 (MVac restart)

target_perigee_km.src: https://celestrak.org/NORAD/elements/supplemental/sup-gp.php?FILE=starlink-g15-16&FORMAT=json deploy orbit 252.1 x 264.7 km (SpaceX pre-launch state vector)

burns.basis: timing from SpaceX timeline; thrust solved (throttle unpublished) so the 2 s burn raises perigee to the SpaceX/CelesTrak deploy perigee 252.1 km.

notes: CelesTrak SupGP deploy-state epoch 05:47:17Z = T+3737 s, 24 s after SpaceX's published deploy; SpaceX time used.
Perigee/apogee are osculating (r - 6378.137 km) and will differ by a few km from CelesTrak mean elements.
